llm.summary: The skill claims a paid banner-generation flow but its payment/credential handling and runtime instructions are inconsistent (and it asks the model to disclose its internal thinking), so you should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose (generate team-banner slogans, paid service) matches the included scripts (order creation, banner generation). However the SKILL.md declares payment processing, network outbound, and credential.read permissions while the Python scripts perform only local file I/O and do not contact payment endpoints. The skill asks users to configure a merchant ID in configs/config.json — that is expected — but declaring network/credential permissions appears disproportionate unless an external 'clawtip' skill actually handles network payments.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md requires the agent to interact in Chinese and to include its 'thinking process' (chain-of-thought), which is a privacy/policy concern and grants overly broad discretion. The doc mandates a two-step flow (create order → use 'clawtip' to collect payCredential → run banner generation), but the banner_generate.py script only checks for a local order file and does not validate any payCredential or payment status. This is a functional mismatch: the instructions require payment verification but the code does not enforce it, enabling potential bypasses.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external install/spec that downloads code from remote URLs; the skill is instruction+local Python scripts only. No non-standard install behavior or remote extract was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, and stores configuration in configs/config.json (which in the provided bundle already contains payTo and sm4Key). Declaring credential.read in SKILL.md is not reflected by required.env. The presence of sm4Key and a long payTo value in the bundled config is sensitive information stored in repo files — if these are real credentials they should not be checked into the skill manifest. Overall, requested environment/credential access is not proportional to the actual local-file-only implementation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes order files under the user's home directory (~/.openclaw/... or Windows equivalent). It does not set always:true, does not modify other skills, nor request system-wide privileges. Persistent storage of orders is expected for the purpose.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill bundles local Python scripts that implement a simple paid workflow but the documentation and code disagree in important ways. Before installing: (1) Do not accept the instruction that the agent should reveal its internal 'thinking' — remove that requirement. (2) Inspect and, if needed, remove any real credentials from configs/config.json; do not commit real merchant keys or encryption keys into the skill files. (3) Verify how payment is actually enforced: banner_generate.py does not validate a payCredential, so payment could be bypassed by creating an order file manually. (4) If you will use an external payment skill (clawtip), audit that skill and its required credentials separately. (5) If you need strict payment enforcement, modify the code to require and verify a payCredential (and avoid storing secrets in plaintext). If you want, I can suggest concrete code changes to validate payments and remove the chain-of-thought instruction.
